focus.jbig: Record Nasdaq, calm VIX, 5.28% yields, $88 oil, active war · FOMC minutes 2 ET · zero names boarded
focus.jtag: Tech led to a record Nasdaq and oil is easing, but an active US–Iran war, a 24-year-high bond market and $88 oil keep the tape two-sided — the scanner found no qualifying setups
focus.jnote: The surface is strong but the floor is not. The Nasdaq closed at a fresh record Monday (up ~1.05%), the S&P added ~0.66% to ~7,774 and futures are higher again as megacap tech — Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta — keeps powering the tape and oil slides on recovering Gulf exports. But three live wires remain: the US–Israel war on Iran drags on with the Strait of Hormuz still blockaded and tankers being struck; the 10Y sits near ~5.28%, easing only slightly after hitting a fresh 24-year high Monday; and oil near $88 (Brent near $98–100) even as Mideast exports recover above pre-war levels. Gold is holding ~$4,120–4,170. FOMC minutes land at 2:00 ET. This is a headline-and-rate tape, not one a Sniper sells premium into — and the scanner confirmed it: zero names cleared the criteria today.
focus.notdown: Megacap tech & AI (NVDA, MSFT, META) led the market to a record Nasdaq — but that’s momentum and stretched leadership, not a durable, named catalyst, and a single AI-name wobble can gap the whole index. Energy (XLE, XOM, CVX, OXY) still carries a war-premium bid, but oil actually fell again today on recovering Gulf exports, showing this is a two-sided supply-shock trade, not a clean Sniper. One de-escalation or export-normalization headline and crude gives back more premium. Watch-only. Nothing here cleared validation.
focus.notup: Rate-sensitive groups (REITs, utilities, housing, small caps) stay pressured with the 10Y near ~5.28% and oil feeding inflation fear. But selling bear calls into a VIX this low, with a record-chasing tape that can squeeze shorts on any fresh tech or de-escalation headline, carries its own violent-reversal risk — the disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why RED? Composite ~51 is in WARM and P(≥1% gap) at 37% is above the 35% trigger — either one alone locks out GREEN. More important than the numbers: an active military conflict with oil still near $88 is an unscheduled, open-ended tail, stacked on a bond market at ~5.28% 24-year-high yields and FOMC minutes at 2:00 ET. The full-universe scanner ran successfully and boarded ZERO names. A record Nasdaq and a low VIX are not a green light when the gap tail is headline-driven and skewed. Stand down on new credit spreads, or push DTE past the headline window and cut size hard. Cash is a position today.

risks: US–Israel war on Iran & the Strait of Hormuz — the strait remains blockaded, tankers have been struck repeatedly in recent days, and Trump has said a decision on Iran is imminent. Any strike on Gulf oil infrastructure or personnel gaps the whole tape instantly. This is the number-one thing to watch.

Bond yields — 10Y near ~5.28%, just off fresh 24-year highs — the 10Y and 30-year both hit levels not seen since 2002 on Monday before easing. Hawkish FOMC minutes or a hot inflation read could send yields back up and hit rate-sensitive growth, REITs, utilities and small caps hardest.

Oil near $88 / Brent near $98–100 — crude is easing as Gulf exports recover above pre-war levels, but the move is two-sided; any fresh disruption to Hormuz shipping sends crude (and jet fuel) vertical and feeds inflation fear.
FOMC minutes · today 2:00 ET — with the market reading a Fed hold after soft jobs and PCE, a hawkish tone in the minutes could revive yield pressure; a dovish read supports the Fed-hold trade.

Q3 earnings start this week — PepsiCo (Thu 10/8) and Delta (Fri 10/9) open the season, then the big banks ~10/13–14, stacking single-stock gap risk on an already-edgy macro tape. Keep every spread clear of its name’s print.
